summary: Preflight validated the approved guest/x64dbg environment and guest-only execution workflow. Upstream Pass 1 plus host PE triage show the sample is a directly analyzable PE32 service DLL with ordinary sections/imports and no credible startup packer or self-decoding evidence, so unpacking was not needed. A guest debug smoke test reached x64dbg but loaded the DLL through DLLLoader32_0E62.exe rather than the natural svchost service context, so no unpack rounds or recovered artifacts were produced; cleanup succeeded and the guest was reverted to VMRunV4.

findings.title: Preflight validated the approved guest-only execution path and required debugger tools
findings.description: The unpack stage safety gate was satisfied: the approved VMware guest and VMRunV4 snapshot were present, the x64dbg MCP health endpoint was reachable, required debug, memory, and dump tools were enumerated, and the prepared workflow used guest file copy plus guest-side x64dbg launch rather than host execution.
findings.reasoning: The prepare-env report recorded host-to-guest copy and guest x64dbg launch for this sample. During this stage, healthcheck.py returned an OK status from the x64dbg MCP endpoint, initialize/tools/list exposed the required runtime and dump tools, and vmrun confirmed the approved VMX plus VMRunV4 snapshot. This is sufficient to validate the environment before making the unpack decision.

sources.location: scripts/healthcheck.py; tools/list; vmrun listSnapshots; vmrun list

evidence.observation: scripts/healthcheck.py returned OK 200 from http://192.168.248.169:3000 with body {"status":"ok","service":"x64dbg-mcp"}.

MCP initialize returned serverInfo.name x64dbg-mcp version 1.0.7, and tools/list exposed debug_init, debug_get_state, module_get_main, symbol_resolve, memory_enumerate, memory_get_info, dump_analyze_module, dump_get_dumpable_regions, dump_memory_region, and dump_module.

The prepare-env report recorded CopyFileFromHostToGuest of the sample to C:\Users\h26v\Desktop\000d1bab5fa789f2d3b120bccb5452c7c3fe52073bd88d7d651b27dc68eb5423 and guest launch of C:\Users\h26v\Downloads\x64dbg\release\x96dbg.exe with that guest-side copy.
vmrun listSnapshots for H:\VMware\WinVM\Windows 10 - RunSmt.vmx showed snapshot VMRunV4, and vmrun list showed that same VMX as the active guest before cleanup.

limitations: Tooling validation does not by itself reproduce the sample's intended svchost-hosted service context.

findings.title: No credible startup packing or self-decoding evidence was observed
findings.description: The sample remained directly analyzable as a normal PE32 DLL with standard sections and a populated import directory, and no packer-specific or startup self-unpacking signals met the threshold for an unpack round.
findings.reasoning: Pass 1 already described a conventional service DLL and explicitly stated that no standard packer or staged in-memory unpack stub was confirmed. Host-side PE triage in this stage independently found a normal MZ/PE image with .text, .rdata, .data, .rsrc, and .reloc sections plus a non-empty import directory. Under the stage decision policy, that makes unpacking unnecessary.

evidence.observation: Pass 1 recorded a conventional PE32 DLL layout, ordinary CRT startup through DllEntryPoint, and no observed RWX unpack loop, relocation fixer, or import-reconstruction handoff in the startup path.

Host PE triage parsed a 208896-byte PE32 image with entrypoint RVA 0x12faa, image base 0x64000000, five standard sections (.text, .rdata, .data, .rsrc, .reloc), and an import directory at RVA 0x2b0ac with size 160.

limitations: This decision does not exclude later network-delivered secondary content; it only addresses startup packing and unpack recovery for the supplied sample.

findings.title: Direct guest debugging used x64dbg's DLL loader helper instead of the natural service host
findings.description: A guest debug smoke test reached x64dbg successfully, but the resulting main module was DLLLoader32_0E62.exe rather than the sample's intended svchost-hosted service context described in Pass 1.
findings.reasoning: The supplied target is a DLL, so x64dbg's direct launch path used a helper executable to host it. That behavior is acceptable for debugger reachability checks, but it is not the correct context for validating service-host runtime behavior or searching for a service-specific unpack handoff.

evidence.observation: Immediately after launch, module_get_main reported the main module as dllloader32_0e62.exe at C:\Users\h26v\Desktop\DLLLoader32_0E62.exe with base 0x0000000000820000 and entry 0x00000000008213C9.

The initial module list contained dllloader32_0e62.exe plus apphelp.dll, kernelbase.dll, kernel32.dll, and ntdll.dll, which is consistent with a helper-hosted DLL debug session rather than a service-hosted svchost trace.

limitations: This observation should not be used as proof of the sample's natural runtime module graph under svchost.exe.

findings.title: Debugger cleanup and guest revert completed successfully
findings.description: After the decision-only unpack stage, the debugger session was stopped and the VMware guest was powered off and reverted so no guest analysis process remained running.
findings.reasoning: The skill requires cleanup regardless of whether unpacking is needed. debug_stop returned success true, the stop-and-revert vmrun sequence completed without error output, and a final vmrun list showed zero running VMs.

sources.location: debug_stop; vmrun stop; vmrun revertToSnapshot; vmrun list

evidence.observation: The x64dbg MCP debug_stop call returned {"success": true}.
After stop-and-revert, vmrun list reported Total running VMs: 0.

investigation_targets.target: Service-hosted runtime under svchost.exe instead of DLLLoader32_0E62.exe
investigation_targets.reason: Pass 1 identifies a svchost-hosted service DLL, but the unpack-stage debug smoke test used x64dbg's helper loader and therefore did not validate the natural runtime context.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: If deeper runtime analysis is needed, run the later behavior/dynamic workflow under the approved guest path that loads the sample through its intended service host or verified wkssvc proxy scenario rather than x64dbg's generic DLL loader.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Observe svchost.exe hosting, worker-thread launch, resolved wkssvc forwards/endpoints, and confirm whether any later in-memory payload unpacking occurs.

investigation_targets.target: Decoded network task buffers after protocol processing
investigation_targets.reason: Pass 1 indicates custom-framed network exchanges and a CreateProcessW-compatible handoff, so any future secondary artifact is more likely to appear after network decode than at process startup.
investigation_targets.recommended_action: Instrument the protocol decode and task-execution path in a later dynamic stage instead of repeating startup unpack attempts.
investigation_targets.success_criteria: Recover decoded task or command data and determine whether it contains an executable PE/raw payload or only behavior or command strings.

limitations: Direct x64dbg launch of the DLL used a helper executable and did not reproduce the sample's intended svchost-hosted service context.
No unpack artifact was generated because startup packing evidence was not observed; later runtime work should focus on behavior validation rather than unpack recovery.
The stage stopped after the unpack decision and safety validation, so it did not attempt recovery of any network-delivered secondary content.
